Author: Farjand Ali Bench: Farjand Ali [2025:RJ-JD:22546]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Misc Suspension Of Sentence Application (Appeal)
 No. 1302/2022 Laxman Lal S/o Shri Ratan Lal Bhil, Aged About 20 Years, R/o Tejya Khedi, Tan Narayan Kheda, Thana Raipur, District Bhilwara.

sentences.text:
(At Present Lodged In Central Jail Ajmer)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Kaluram Bhati  Mr. Amardeep Lamba For Respondent(s) : Mr. Shrawan Singh Rathore, DyGA  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE FARJAND ALI Order 08/05/2025 1.

The instant application for suspension of sentence has been moved on behalf of the appellant-applicant in the matter of judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 30.11.2019 passed by the learned Special Judge, POCSO Act Cases No.2, Bhilwara in Sessions Case No.26/2019 (10/2019) whereby he was convicted for the offences under Sections 376 (3) of the IPC and Sections 3/4 of the POCSO Act and has been awarded sentence of rigorous imprisonment of 20 years alongwith fine and default sentence.

entities.text: Special Judge, POCSO Act Cases No.2, Bhilwara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. It is contended by the learned counsel for the appellant that the learned trial Judge has not appreciated the correct, legal and factual aspects of the matter and thus, reached at an erroneous conclusion of guilt, therefore, the same is required to be [2025:RJ-JD:22546] (2 of 4)
[SOSA-1302/2022] appreciated again by this court being the first appellate Court.
The appellant has strong arguable case in his favour.
He has remain incarcerated for a period of nearly 7 years, but hearing of the appeal is likely to take long time, therefore, the application for suspension of sentence may be granted.

sentences.text: 3. Per contra, learned public prosecutor has vehemently opposed the prayer made by learned counsel for the accused- applicant for releasing the appellant on application for suspension of sentence.
4. As per the report received by the learned Public Prosecutor, the victim/complainant has been intimated regarding hearing of the bail plea.
However, no one is present on his/her behalf to contest the bail plea.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
6.
A perusal of the record is revealing that the appellant has served a period of nearly 7 years out of the total sentence of 20 years.
At the time of the alleged offence, the appellant was a young boy aged 19 years.
Learned counsel for the appellant has pointed out number of discrepancies in the prosecution case, more particularly regarding the age of the victim.

Being the first appellate court,
when the appeal has been admitted, this court is duty bound to make a critical legal and factual appreciation of the material brought on record.
There is no likelihood of hearing of the appeal on an early date.

Thus, considering the submissions advanced at bar, grounds raised in the memo of appeal and looking to the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, while refraining from passing any comments on the niceties of the [2025:RJ-JD:22546] (3 of 4) [SOSA-1302/2022]
matter and the defects of the prosecution as the same may put an adverse effect on hearing of the appeal, this court is of the opinion that it is a fit case for suspending the sentence awarded to the accused-appellant.

7. Accordingly, the application for suspension of sentence filed under Section 389 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the sentence passed by learned trial court, details of which are mentioned in opening para of this order, against the appellant- applicant named above shall remain suspended till final disposal of the aforesaid appeal and he shall be released on bail provided he executes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance in this court on 06.06.2025 and whenever ordered to do so till the disposal of the appeal on the conditions indicated below:-
1. That he will appear before the trial Court in the month of January of every year till the appeal is decided.
2. That if the applicant changes the place of residence, he will give in writing his changed address to the trial Court as well as to the counsel in the High Court.
3. Similarly, if the sureties change their address(s), they will give in writing their changed address to the trial Court.
8. The learned trial Court shall keep the record of attendance of the accused-applicant in a separate file.
Such file be registered as Criminal Misc. Case related to original case in which the accused- applicant was tried and convicted.
A copy of this order shall also be placed in that file for ready reference.
